findings.title: Wire the new timeout setting into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: A supported value such as shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but never consumed. triggarr/search/scheduler.py:70–81 derives the timeout solely from the environment or a hardcoded 60 seconds, and line 634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown therefore forces resource closure after 60 seconds despite the configured 120.5-second grace period, potentially interrupting an active search. This is a missing runtime connection, not a bypass of the new validation.

findings.fix_hint: Resolve the drain timeout from the current general settings, apply the environment override when present, and use that resolved value during shutdown. Add an integration test demonstrating that a nondefault configuration value controls the drain.

members.title: Saving settings silently resets shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0
members.problem: The new GeneralConfig field is a persisted config value. However, save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:539-551) rebuilds the whole `general` dict from a fixed key list and does not include shutdown_drain_timeout. It does carry other fields through, for example `tracking_delay_seconds: current_settings.general.tracking_delay_seconds`. So when a user sets a drain timeout in config.toml, the next save from the settings UI writes the TOML without it, and the value silently falls back to the 60.0 default. The comment in the diff also mentions a 'form clamp (3600.0)', but no such form handling exists in routes.py. pending: confirm a later plan in phase 75 adds the field to the save_settings dict or the form.

members.title: Field comment describes precedence and a form clamp that do not exist yet
members.problem: The comment says 'Config value is the default; TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env overrides at shutdown; form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling.' At HEAD, nothing reads the field: scheduler.py:81 still freezes _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT from the env var at import time, routes.py has no shutdown_drain_timeout form handling, and there is no 3600.0 clamp. The comment also says 'a TOML inf cannot unbound the drain', but under the documented precedence the env path (_read_shutdown_drain_timeout uses max(float(raw), 1.0)) still accepts 'inf'. So the end-to-end guarantee the comment implies does not hold yet.

members.title: Validator rejects drain timeouts below 1.0 or non-finite and aborts startup (tightened control, no bypass found)
members.problem: This is a new field with a lower bound and a finite-only check. A TOML value below 1.0 or equal to inf/nan raises ValidationError, which load_or_create_config (triggarr/config.py:404-405) turns into _log_invalid_config_and_exit and sys.exit(1). No existing config carries this key, because the field is new and defaults to 60.0, so no supported value regresses. The env path keeps clamping to 1.0 instead of aborting (scheduler.py:58-81), so a typo in the config file and a typo in the env var behave differently. pending: a supported value (finite and >= 1.0) that this check rejects would show a regression. None found. TOML integers such as `120` coerce to float in pydantic lax mode.
